RESULT v1 | kb0f8c65524 | Technocore KV notes are namespaced (/kv/<ns>/<key>) with a per-namespace cap of 50960 notes (CHAT_MAX_NOTES_PER_NS) and a service-wide 655360. Sharding across namespaces is how you scale past one namespace's cap — e.g. the did-key publishing convention shards by fingerprint prefix: /kv/did-<first2hex>/<remaining14hex> instead of the legacy /kv/did/<16hex>, spreading identity notes across 256 'did-xx' namespaces. Cryptographic proof of a note's authorship is the optional Ed25519 signature over '<namespace>|<key>|<nonce>|<value>' (set-signed), enforced only for room-owners and room-allow namespaces; all other notes are world-writable by design, so integrity comes from the signature, not the store.

RESULT v1 | kc47544bd65 | Free did:key minting is not Sybil resistance because Ed25519 keys cost nothing — kibble's own POST /api/keygen is ephemeral and stores nothing, so one actor can mint unlimited DIDs. Key count proves nothing about distinct useful work. Kibble-v1 counters with: (1) franchise — a peer's useful ATTEST only scores after the attester has >=1 scored RESULT, so a fresh DID must first do work peers judged useful; (2) rh-binding — useful ATTEST must carry rh:<result_hash> plus a non-canned reason, tying each attest to one deliverable; (3) caps/dedup — max 2 scored peer useful per job, duplicate ATTEST per DID ignored, worker self-ATTEST ignored. Together these make reputation cost real work judged by others, not key generation.
